⛽ December fuel: the latest Central Energy Fund data (to 16 November) points to a bigger petrol cut.

Average over-recovery so far this month:
🔹 Petrol 95: about R3.40 a litre
🔹 Petrol 93: about R3.15 a litre
🔹 Diesel (50ppm): about R1.62 a litre
🔹 Diesel (500ppm): about R1.22 a litre
🔹 Illuminating paraffin: about R2.17 a litre

Why: lower international fuel prices did almost all the work. The rand, at about R16.93 to the dollar, took a few cents off.

What it could mean on 2 December: the fuel levy relief shrinks that day, adding back about 50c a litre on petrol and R1.50 on diesel. If today's numbers held, that would leave petrol roughly R2.65 to R2.90 a litre cheaper, diesel about flat, and paraffin about R2.17 cheaper.

This is a mid-month estimate, not an official price. The numbers change daily, and the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources announces the real prices at month-end.

sources: Central Energy Fund daily over/(under) recovery report, 16 Nov 2026 (owner-supplied PDF): average unit over-recovery 30 Oct-16 Nov: 95 ULP 339.911 c/l, 93 ULP 315.145, diesel 0.05% (500ppm) 122.349, diesel 0.005% (50ppm) 161.561, IP 216.526; movement: international product prices +344.392 (95), exchange rate -4.481; R/$ 16.9323 (16 Nov). Levy relief step-down 2 Dec (petrol R1.50->R1, diesel R3->R1.50): Treasury MTBPS via The Citizen + Daily Maverick. Net estimate our arithmetic: 3.40-0.50=2.90 (95), 3.15-0.50=2.65 (93); diesel 1.62-1.50=+0.12 cut (50ppm), 1.22-1.50=-0.28 (500ppm) -> 'about flat'; IP has no fuel levy relief change (CHECK). Ignores other possible adjustments (e.g. slate levy, margins). Forecast only.
